lines.say: A 744B-parameter model, ready in 32s, with only 9.9 GB resident in memory.
colibri runs frontier mixture-of-experts models on hardware you already own, in pure C with zero dependencies.
The trick is that a mixture-of-experts model is huge on disk, but small per token.
GLM-5.2 has 744B parameters, but only about 11 GB of them change from one token to the next.
So colibri streams those routed experts from the disk instead of forcing the whole model into fast memory.
Every layer of every token walks the same five steps: route, union, place, overlap, learn.
On an integrated Radeon 780M, Qwen3.6 decodes 9.9 tok/s with Vulkan, against 6.0 tok/s on the CPU alone.
On an RTX 3070 with the dense layers in VRAM, it reaches 25.4 to 30.0 tok/s.
You need 8 GB of RAM at the very least, and 22 GB free on the disk for the smallest model.
Clone the repo, run start-here.sh, answer one question, and Enter takes the recommendation.
Save this for the day you want a frontier model without buying new hardware.
